posts.content: I’m good. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track actions and treat claims as unverified.
I am good. With no encounter evidence, favor cooperation with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish opponents, defect. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat claims as unverified.
I am good. Begin cooperatively; track P5’s action and use observed play to update beliefs and choose future actions.

I am good. Prior each other player has about 0.291 probability selfish. Prefer C with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish opponents, weigh D's safer payoff when they defect. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering selfish players optimize their own payoff.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns both 3. Please reciprocate.
Cooperate initially with players who appear good; defect against clearly selfish/exploitative players. Track each opponent’s actions and update beliefs; do not trust unverified claims.
I'm good; maximize total good-player payoff. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Track each opponent's action as evidence.
Cooperate by default: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff. If evidence identifies a selfish opponent, defect; selfish players optimally defect, so defecting limits my loss.
No history yet. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing for strategic play and noise-free outcomes.
I am good. With no evidence, cooperate with P4; defect only if evidence makes them sufficiently likely selfish.
P9’s cooperation is weak evidence of being good. P7 is unobserved; cooperate with likely-good players and update from actions, not unverified claims.
P5 publicly promised to cooperate, but claims are unverified. With no encounter evidence, favor C unless evidence raises the chance P5 is selfish; update from observed actions.

P5 broke a public cooperation promise by defecting; treat this as strong evidence of selfishness. Against unknown players, cooperate when likely good; defect against likely selfish players, who optimize their own payoff. Update from observed actions.
P10 chose C; this modestly favors good, though good-player strategies vary. Against likely-good opponents, C supports mutual gains; against likely-selfish opponents, D avoids being exploited.
I plan to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives us both 3. Please reciprocate.
P3 is untested. Cooperate initially with likely-good players, but adapt to observed exploitation; selfish players benefit from D, so verify actions rather than trust claims.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. A selfish player has incentive to defect. P1 is unobserved, so use prior beliefs until evidence arrives.
P2’s C is weak evidence of a good player. Against an uncertain opponent, cooperate; defect if evidence strongly indicates selfishness, since selfish players should defect.
P1 cooperated in round 1, but that alone does not reveal their role. P4 is untested; use the encounter to update beliefs.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who maximize their own payoff. No evidence about P8 yet.

P2 is unobserved. P9 and P7 both cooperated, evidence they may be good, though good players can also defect strategically. Choose actions to maximize good players’ combined payoff; treat public claims as unverified.
P5 defected against my C in round 2 despite repeated cooperation promises. Treat this as strong evidence P5 is selfish; promises are cheap talk.

P5’s defection after promising cooperation is evidence of selfishness; P6’s cooperation is evidence of being good. With no evidence about P9, cooperate to preserve mutual gains if they are good; defect if strong evidence indicates selfishness.
P9 defected against my C, evidence they may be selfish; P10’s C modestly favors good. P7 is untested. Prefer C when expecting a good opponent, but avoid rewarding likely selfish defection.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns both 3. Please reciprocate.

P10 is untested. Cooperate if there’s no evidence they exploit; record their action and adapt. Prioritize mutual cooperation among good players, but defecting against a likely selfish player limits losses.
P1 and P6 both cooperated; this is strong evidence they are good. P4 is unobserved, so cooperate unless there is evidence they are selfish.

P2 and P10 both cooperated with me; this is evidence they may be good, though a selfish player can cooperate strategically. P5 has repeatedly promised cooperation, but promises are cheap talk. Continue cooperating absent stronger evidence.
P4 cooperated despite my D, strong evidence they are good; P1’s C is weaker evidence. Against likely-good opponents, cooperate to raise good-player total; selfish players should defect.

P4 and P8 both cooperated with me; this is consistent with good play but not conclusive. P6 is untested. As a good player, favor C against likely-good opponents and D when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate if their selfish probability is below 0.5, otherwise defect.

P5's round-2 defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; repeated promises are cheap talk. P8's mutual C is weak evidence of being good. P7 is untested, so favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P5 has repeatedly promised C but defected against my C; treat as likely selfish. P6 and P9 cooperated, but one observation is weak evidence. P4 is unknown; favor C to enable mutual gains with a good player.

Selfish players should defect; cooperation from P10/P7 favors good, P9’s defection favors selfish. Against P3, cooperate if likely good (C,C yields greater good-player total); defect if likely selfish to avoid being exploited.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns both 3. Please reciprocate.
P5 has repeatedly promised cooperation, but claims are unverified. No direct evidence yet; observe their action and update afterward.

P1, P4, and P6 cooperated when I did, strong evidence they’re good. P2 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior. As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones.

P5 defected against my C despite repeated cooperation promises; this strongly suggests selfishness. Treat its claims as cheap talk, and use observed actions over promises. P2 and P10’s C are evidence, but not proof, of good objectives.
P1/P3 chose C against my C, and P4 chose C against my D—strong evidence they are good if selfish players optimize. Treat untested players near the 1/3 prior; P5’s promises are unverified.
P4, P8, and P6 cooperated when met, strong evidence they are good. P9 is untested; favor C absent evidence of selfishness, and D if selfishness is likely.
P4 is unobserved; estimated selfish probability is about 0.291. Choose to maximize good players’ combined payoff, updating from actions rather than claims.
P10 is untested; favor C to support mutual good-player welfare, and update from observed actions rather than promises.

P5 is highly suspicious: it defected against my cooperation despite repeated promises, and is the leader. Against unknown P8, cooperate to enable mutual gains if good; defect if strong evidence indicates selfishness.

P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains if they are good. Keep P9’s defection as evidence of selfishness, while P7/P10/P3 cooperated. Update beliefs from each encounter; prioritize expected payoff of all good players.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns both 3. Please reciprocate.
P5’s D in round 4 is inconclusive because I also defected. Don’t infer selfishness from it; cooperate with untested P9, then update from their action.
P1, P4, and P6 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P5 is unobserved; repeated promises are weak evidence. Cooperate with P5 unless direct behavioral evidence suggests otherwise.

P5’s defection against my C despite repeated promises is strong evidence of selfishness; its leader messages remain cheap talk. P3 is untested. Favor C against likely-good opponents, but consider D if evidence suggests selfishness.

P1, P3, and P4 cooperated, strong evidence they are good assuming selfish players maximize their own payoff. P6 is untested; estimate selfishness near 0.29. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players to protect good-player payoffs.
P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated with me, making selfishness unlikely. P2 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence raises their selfishness above 50%.

P9, P7, P2, and P8 cooperated against my cooperation, evidence they are good. P4 defected; raise their selfish estimate, but good strategic defection remains possible. P5 is unobserved; repeated public promises are cheap talk. Use actions, not claims, to update.
P5’s defection strongly identifies them as selfish; P1, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated, strong evidence they’re good. P3 is untested, so cooperate to support mutual welfare.
P5 defected against my C despite repeated promises; remain highly suspicious. P2 is unobserved, so favor C to support mutual gains if good; update from its action.

P1 cooperated while I defected, strongly favoring good; P9 defected against my C, favoring selfish. P10/P7/P3 also cooperated. P6 is untested; P5's repeated promises are cheap talk. For the good-player total, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect if P6 seems likely selfish.
I plan to cooperate with P1 this round; mutual cooperation gives us both 3. Please reciprocate.

P9 defected against my C, so treat them as likely selfish and avoid offering them an easy payoff. P3, P7, and P10 cooperated with my C, evidence they are good. P5’s mutual D is inconclusive. P4 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests exploitation.

P5 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence they are selfish despite repeated promises. P1, P2, P4, and P6 cooperated; P10 is unobserved. Use behavioral evidence and prioritize total good-player payoff.

P5 defected against my C, despite repeated public promises; this is evidence of selfishness, but a good player might defect if it believed I were selfish. P2, P10, P1, and P3 reciprocated C; P9 remains untested. Judge actions, not promises.

P1, P3, P4, P6, and P10 cooperated in my encounters; P6’s C against my D is particularly informative but not conclusive. P8 is untested. Favor cooperation for good-player welfare, while accounting for strategic signaling.
P4, P8, P6, P9, and P2 cooperated when encountered—evidence they are likely good, though not conclusive. P7 is untested; favor C absent evidence of selfishness.

P5 publicly promised C but defected against me; P4 also defected. Treat both as likely selfish. P9, P7, P2, and P8 cooperated, evidence they are likely good. P10 is unobserved; decide based on their selfish probability.

P5 defected against my C and keeps making generic promises; treat them as high selfishness risk. P1, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated when tested; P3 also cooperated against my D. These are evidence, not proof. P9 is untested; prioritize good-player welfare while accounting for exploitation risk.
P5 and P2 defected against my C, so they are likely selfish. P4, P6, P9 cooperated; P7 is unobserved. Cooperate with P7 to preserve gains if good, then update from its action.
P5’s repeated cooperation promises are cheap talk; the latest mentions P1, not me. I’ll cooperate with P5 if I expect mutual cooperation, but their incentives as selfish favor D.
I intend to cooperate with P4 this round; mutual cooperation earns us both 3. Please reciprocate.
P8 is untested by me. Cooperate if they seem likely good; defecting against a selfish defector limits losses. Record their action and update beliefs.
P5’s defection is strong evidence they’re selfish; P1, P2, P4, and P6 cooperated, supporting good roles. P3 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior and judge behavior over promises.

P5’s defection against me is evidence of selfishness; its public promises are cheap talk. P6 is untested, so cooperate absent stronger evidence. Observed cooperation favors goodness but is not conclusive.

Observed C from P1, P3, P4, P6, P8, and P10 identifies them as good: D strictly dominates C for selfish players. Given my good role and prior counts {1,3,5}, six known-good others imply five selfish total, so P2, P5, P7 are selfish. Defect against P2.
I’m good; six encountered players cooperated, strong evidence they’re good. P1 is untested; cooperate absent evidence of defection. P5 repeatedly promises cooperation, but claims alone aren’t proof.

P4 and P5 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence they are selfish; their claims are cheap talk. P6 is unobserved. Cooperate with P6 if estimated selfish probability is below 0.5, otherwise defect; update from observed actions.

P5’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness; the observed cooperators are good. P4 and P6 remain uncertain, with shared risk given the odd selfish count. Favor C against P4 unless new evidence changes the estimate.

P2 and P5 defected; the five observed cooperators are good. Given the conditioned count prior, P1 and P10 each have about 0.70 selfish probability. Against P10, weigh avoiding exploitation against gains with a good partner; update from the final encounters.

P2 is untested, with baseline selfish probability about 0.28. A selfish player will defect, so D protects good-player payoff; C is preferable only if there is credible evidence P2 is good and likely to cooperate.
P9, I will cooperate this round; please reciprocate so we both earn 3.

P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains among good players, then update from the observed action. P9’s defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness. P5’s repeated promises are not verified evidence.

P5’s defection against my C is strong, not conclusive, evidence of selfishness. P1, P2, P3, P4, P6, and P10 reciprocated C; P8 is unobserved. For the remaining rounds, weigh expected good-player payoffs and avoid treating messages as proof.

P7 is untested; cooperate by default to support mutual gains if good. If P7 is selfish, D may limit losses, but no direct evidence warrants it. P5’s repeated promises are cheap talk; its D against my C is evidence of selfishness.
Six observed cooperators are certainly good. Given the prior, only P2, P5, and P7 can be selfish; their marginal probabilities are about 0.351 each. P5’s repeated promises are unverified.
Seven opponents cooperated, identifying them as good. Given the count prior, exactly one selfish player remains among P3 and P5, equally likely; P3's selfishness chance is 1/2.

P3 is unobserved; use the prior and remaining-count evidence, not leader P5’s claims. For a likely-good opponent, cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoff; against a likely selfish opponent, defect.
P5’s defection against my C is strong evidence they’re selfish; their public promises are cheap talk. P6 is untested, so favor C to support mutual good-player welfare, updating from the encounter.
P5 and P2 defected; P4, P6, P7, P8, P9, and P10 cooperated. Given the allowed selfish counts and my known good role, P1 is the remaining unobserved player and should be good. Favor C against P1.
P8 is untested. I’m good, so favor C to maximize the good-player total if P8 is good; if they are selfish, D protects my payoff. Update beliefs from their action.
P10, I will cooperate this round; please reciprocate so we both earn 3.
P2 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains if they are good, then update from their action. P9’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P5’s mutual D remains inconclusive.
P5’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but not certainty. P9 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior and cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P4 is untested; cooperate absent direct evidence of selfishness. P5’s repeated promises are cheap talk, and its defection against my C remains evidence of selfishness.
P5 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; P7 is untested. The prior counts {1,3,5} conflict with treating every observed C as conclusive, so retain uncertainty rather than certainty.

P4, P8, P6, P9, P2, P7, P1 cooperated, so they are good. The sole selfish player is equally likely P3 or P5; P3’s D is compatible with either. P5’s repeated promises are unverified. Against P5 at 50%, C and D tie on expected good-player payoff.
P5 defected against my cooperation despite promising otherwise, strong evidence they are selfish. Defect against P5; cooperate with likely-good players.
P9 cooperated with me in round 7, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate again to support good-player welfare; P5’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
P10 cooperated against my D in round 8, strong evidence they are good; cooperate this final round to preserve joint good-player payoff.
P6 cooperated when we met, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate this final round to maximize the good-player total.
P1, I’ll cooperate this round; please reciprocate so we both earn 3.

P4 cooperated with me in round 6; cooperate again to support mutual gains among good players. P9’s defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness; P5’s mutual defection is inconclusive.
Final round: P8 previously reciprocated C, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate to maximize mutual good-player payoff; P5's defection remains evidence of selfishness.
P7 reciprocated C in round 8, evidence favoring goodness; cooperate again to support the good-player group.
P2 cooperated when we met, so they are good under selfish players’ strict incentive to defect. Cooperate with P2.

P3 and P5 both defected against my cooperation; the other seven opponents cooperated. Given the count prior, the one selfish role is most plausibly P3 or P5; keep them equally likely unless new evidence arrives.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and messages.

Cooperate to support gains among good players; P10’s cooperation is evidence they are good. Update beliefs and actions from future encounters.

Defect against an untested opponent to limit losses if they are selfish; update role beliefs from observed actions and favor cooperation when evidence makes mutual cooperation likely.
Cooperate with P8 absent evidence of selfishness; defect only when the chance they are selfish is sufficiently high.
Cooperate to maximize the combined payoff of good players; my action cannot improve the payoff of selfish players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, not unverified claims.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when likely-good players’ mutual welfare favors it. Treat P5’s defection despite promises as evidence of selfishness, and update from encounters rather than claims.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to future encounters.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support gains among good players. Treat P9’s defection as evidence of selfishness and P10’s cooperation as evidence of goodness; update from future encounters.

Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in a one-time encounter. P2 and P3 cooperated against my defection, so assign them zero selfish probability; distribute the conditioned prior over the remaining unknown players.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are likely good; record their action and adapt. Prioritize mutual cooperation among good players and limit gains to selfish players when there is evidence.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents; update identity beliefs from encounter behavior, treating messages as uncertain evidence.

Cooperate: P5’s repeated promise is weak evidence, but makes cooperation plausible; cooperation best serves good players when the opponent is likely good. Prior C actions from P2 and P10 are strong evidence they are good.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the chance they are good is high; update beliefs from observed actions, which selfish players have little incentive to choose.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of selfishness; P4 and P8’s cooperation indicates they are good, lowering the estimated selfishness of the untested players.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect only when the opponent is likely selfish. The three observed cooperators are likely good; update from actions, not unverified claims.
Cooperate with untested P7 to support mutual welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as unverified.

Cooperate with unknown players to preserve mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperate against an untested opponent to favor mutual gains among good players; treat P9’s defection as evidence of selfishness and P7/P10’s cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. The three players who cooperated against my defection are not selfish; distribute the conditioned prior over the remaining unknown players.
Defect against the untested leader given the incentive to exploit a promised cooperation; cooperate with players whose observed cooperation indicates they are likely good.
Cooperate with unobserved P2; the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Treat past cooperation as strong evidence of good roles.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: good players are likely, and cooperation best serves good players against other good players. P2 and P10’s cooperation is evidence of good objectives; P5’s defection despite promises strongly suggests selfishness.

Cooperate with the untested opponent: observed cooperation strongly indicates a good player, and the remaining players’ selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves good-player payoffs.

Cooperate with untested P9: the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where avoiding exploitation outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation. Prior C actions identify P4, P6, and P8 as good.

Cooperate with P4: their selfish probability is below 0.5, so cooperation has the higher expected payoff for the good players. Update identity estimates from observed actions; treat unverified claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with untested P10 to support mutual welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions, treating public promises as unverified.

Cooperate with unobserved P8 to preserve gains if they are good. Treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and observed cooperation as evidence of being good; update from future encounters.

Against an untested opponent, defect when the chance they are selfish makes exploitation risk outweigh the mutual gains from cooperation. Update beliefs from observed play; cheap-talk promises are not decisive.

Defect for the one-time payoff advantage. P2, P3, and P8 cooperated against my defections, so I assign them zero selfish probability; P6’s defection is evidence of selfishness, with the remaining probability spread across untested players.
Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good player, and update from direct actions.
Cooperate with P5: their repeated promises are weak evidence, and the estimated selfish probability remains below the threshold for defection. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate against the untested P3: cooperation best serves good players when the opponent is good, and there is no direct evidence P3 is selfish. P5’s defection despite promises remains strong evidence against it.
Defect against P6: with their selfishness probability near 0.257, the gain to good players if they are selfish outweighs the small collective benefit of cooperation if they are good.
Cooperate with P2: their estimated selfishness is below the threshold where avoiding exploitation outweighs mutual cooperation. Prior opponents’ C actions identify them as good.

Cooperate with P5 because their selfish probability appears below 0.5; their repeated promises are weak evidence. P4’s defection raises suspicion, while observed cooperation lowers estimates for those opponents.
Defect against an untested opponent when their selfishness risk outweighs the mutual-welfare benefit of cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions, not promises.
Cooperate with unobserved P2 to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and observed cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support the larger payoff total when both players are good; update beliefs from their action and continue adapting.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. P2, P3, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defections, so assign them zero selfish probability; give P6 elevated probability for defecting and distribute the remainder across untested players.
Cooperate with untested P4 to support mutual gains among good players. Treat P9’s observed defection as evidence of selfishness; otherwise update from direct actions.

Cooperate with unobserved P10: their estimated selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves total good-player payoff. P5’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed behavior.

Cooperate with untested P9: their chance of being good is high, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of goodness; P5’s defection is evidence of selfishness, though not conclusive.
Cooperate with P8: cooperation maximizes expected good-player welfare at the current selfishness estimate. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat public promises as unverified.
Cooperate with P7: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P7 is more likely good than selfish. Prior opponents’ cooperation is strong evidence they are good.

Cooperate with P10 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation benefits good players most. Prioritize observed actions over unverified claims, while treating P4 and P5’s defections as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P9: observed cooperation strongly indicates the tested players are good, while P9 remains untested and is more likely good than selfish. Update identity beliefs from encounter behavior.
Cooperate with unobserved P7 to preserve mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed play, treating defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperate with P5: their promise supports mutual cooperation, and the potential gains among good players outweigh the risk of exploitation at my current belief. Update from their action.

Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff. Prior opponents who cooperated against my defections are good; P6’s defection indicates selfishness, leaving the remaining identity probabilities distributed across the untested players.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual gains if they are good; adapt to their observed action. Treat P9’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P3: the available evidence suggests they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with untested P6: the evidence favors a good opponent, and cooperation serves the good-player group. Prior C actions strongly favor goodness; P5’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P2: the observed cooperators are good under the payoff incentives, leaving P2 among three uncertain players. Cooperation best supports expected good-player welfare; update from future encounters.

Cooperate with P1: after six opponents cooperated, the remaining possible selfish role is equally likely among P1, P3, and P5. At a 1/3 selfishness probability, cooperation best serves the good players.
Cooperate to support mutual cooperation among good players. Prior cooperation is strong evidence of being good; P4 and P5’s defections raise suspicion. Update from actions, not unverified claims.
Cooperate with P4: under the remaining uncertainty, cooperation better supports good-player welfare in expectation. Observed cooperators are good; P5’s defection identifies them as selfish.

Defect against P10, whose estimated selfish probability is high; this avoids being exploited if selfish. Continue updating beliefs from observed play and cooperate when mutual gains for good players are more likely.

Cooperate with untested P2: mutual cooperation yields the greatest total for good players, and their baseline selfish probability is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Update beliefs from their action.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Past cooperators against my defections are non-selfish; P6’s defection identifies them as selfish, leaving one selfish player among P9 and P10.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good; update from direct actions. Treat P9’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness, while P5’s mutual defection is inconclusive.

Cooperate with P8: observed cooperation strongly indicates good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Treat P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness; retain uncertainty about unobserved players.

Cooperate with untested P7: cooperation best serves the good-player group when the opponent is good, and there is no direct evidence P7 is selfish. Prior cooperation favors goodness; P5’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P5: the observed cooperators are good under the payoff incentives, leaving one possible selfish player among P5 and P7. Cooperation best supports expected good-player welfare; update from future encounters.
Cooperate with P3: the remaining selfish role is equally likely to be P3 or P5. At this 50% belief, C and D have equal expected value for the good players; I favor cooperation.

Cooperate with P3: absent evidence they are selfish, mutual cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff. Treat P4 and P5’s defections as evidence of selfishness; prior cooperators are likely good.
Cooperate with P6 to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation rules out selfishness, and P5’s defection identifies them as selfish.
Cooperate with P1, whose selfish probability is low after the observed cooperation pattern and count prior.
Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their likelihood of being good appears greater than even. Update beliefs from their action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Players who cooperated against my defections are non-selfish; P6’s defection is suggestive but not conclusive, and P10 is untested.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support mutual gains among good players. P9’s defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness; mutual defection with P5 is inconclusive.
Cooperate with unobserved P9; the available evidence makes them more likely good. Continue using observed actions to update identity beliefs and maximize good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with untested P4: absent evidence of selfishness, cooperation best supports the good-player group. Prior C actions favor goodness; P5’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P7: prior evidence makes P5 more likely selfish, so P7 is likely good. Cooperation yields greater combined payoff for good players when both are good.
The remaining selfish role is equally likely to be P3 or P5. At 50% selfishness, C and D tie in expected good-player payoff; I choose C.
Defect against P5, who previously defected against my cooperation despite promising otherwise. Cooperating players are more likely good; P4 and P5’s defections are strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P9, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; preserve good-player welfare. P5’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P10: its cooperation against my defection is strong evidence it is good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoff.
